entry.title: The schematic is source code
entry.summary: Software earned version control, code review, type checkers and CI. Schematics are still drawings, and their mistakes are still found at the assembly house. CoHDL is my answer: treat the board as a program, and give it a compiler.

entry.title: Same bytes, every time
entry.summary: CoHDL promises that compiling the same source with the same dependencies produces the same output — not equivalent output, the same bytes. This post is about what that promise costs, why hardware demands it anyway, and the day sine and cosine nearly broke it.
